rationale: reversefile is an I/O-bound Shootout C++ benchmark with no static profile available (zero source lines and unknown function count), so the table hedges toward low-cost, broadly safe passes: SUB gets the highest weight since arithmetic/boolean substitution is cheap, correct, and effective on the string/byte manipulation this program performs; SPLIT is weighted to fragment basic blocks and amplify FLA/IBR; FLA and BCF receive moderate weights (with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost penalties) because control-flow flattening and bogus control flow add noticeable overhead that is hard to justify for an I/O-heavy workload whose hot loops are short; IBR and ICALL get balanced weights to obscure call/branch targets and raise static analysis effort without excessive indirect-dispatch cost; IGV is kept moderate since this program has few hot globals; all CorrectnessRisk penalties are kept non-trivial so that passes with transform-induced miscompilation risk are deprioritized, preserving correctness given the absence of profile data to validate per-function behavior.
